title: K-2: Being a Good Friend
desc: Learn about kindness, sharing, and being a good friend.

lessons.title: What Is a Friend?
lessons.content: A friend is someone you care about and enjoy spending time with. Friends share, play together, and help each other. Being a good friend means being kind, listening, and showing you care.

lessons.title: Kindness Matters
lessons.content: Kindness means doing nice things for others. You can smile, say thank you, share your toys, or help someone who is sad. Small acts of kindness make people happy.

lessons.title: Sharing and Taking Turns
lessons.content: Sharing means letting others use things that are yours. Taking turns means waiting for your chance. When you share and take turns, everyone gets a turn to play and have fun.

lessons.title: Saying Sorry
lessons.content: Sometimes we make mistakes. Saying 'I'm sorry' shows you care about the other person's feelings. When you apologize, you are being a good friend.

lessons.title: Including Others
lessons.content: Including others means inviting them to play. If you see someone alone, you can ask them to join your game. Everyone wants to feel included and welcome.

title: K-2: All About Feelings
desc: Learn about different emotions and how to handle them.

lessons.title: What Are Feelings?
lessons.content: Feelings are how you feel inside. Happy, sad, angry, scared, and excited are all feelings. Everyone has feelings, and all feelings are okay.

lessons.title: Happy and Excited
lessons.content: When you are happy, you feel good inside. You might smile, laugh, or want to dance. Being excited means you are very happy and can't wait for something fun.

lessons.title: Sad and Upset
lessons.content: Sometimes we feel sad. You might want to cry or be alone. That is okay. When you feel sad, you can talk to someone you trust or do something that makes you feel better.

lessons.title: Angry and Frustrated
lessons.content: Everyone feels angry sometimes. When you are angry, you can take deep breaths, count to ten, or talk to an adult. Hitting or yelling does not help, but taking a break does.

lessons.title: What to Do With Big Feelings
lessons.content: When feelings are too big, talk to a grown-up you trust. You can also draw, take deep breaths, or ask for a hug. Your feelings are important and it is okay to ask for help.

title: 3-5: Digital Citizenship
desc: Learn how to be safe and responsible online.

lessons.title: What Is Digital Citizenship?
lessons.content: Digital citizenship means being safe, responsible, and kind when using the internet. Just like being a good citizen in your community, you need to be a good citizen online. This means being respectful, protecting your privacy, and knowing what to share.

lessons.title: Online Safety
lessons.content: Never share personal information online, like your full name, address, phone number, or school. Use strong passwords and never share them with anyone except your parents. If something online makes you uncomfortable, tell an adult right away.

lessons.title: Cyberbullying
lessons.content: Cyberbullying is being mean to someone online. This includes sending hurtful messages, spreading rumors, or excluding people. If you see cyberbullying, don't join in. Tell an adult and support the person being bullied.

lessons.title: Digital Footprint
lessons.content: Everything you post online leaves a trace called a digital footprint. Once something is online, it is very hard to remove. Think before you post. Ask yourself: Would I want my family or teacher to see this?

lessons.title: Being a Good Digital Friend
lessons.content: Being kind online is just as important as being kind in person. Send positive messages, don't exclude others from group chats, and respect people's feelings. If you wouldn't say it to their face, don't say it online.

title: 3-5: Money and Saving
desc: Learn the basics of money, saving, and making smart choices.

lessons.title: What Is Money?
lessons.content: Money is what we use to buy things. We earn money by working. Money comes as coins and bills. Each coin and bill has a different value. Pennies are worth 1 cent, nickels 5 cents, dimes 10 cents, and quarters 25 cents.

lessons.title: Needs vs Wants
lessons.content: A need is something you must have to live, like food, water, and shelter. A want is something you would like to have, like a toy or a video game. Understanding the difference helps you make smart money choices.

lessons.title: Why Save Money?
lessons.content: Saving means keeping money instead of spending it right away. You save for things that cost a lot, like a bike. Saving helps you be ready for emergencies and reach your goals. Even saving a little at a time adds up!

lessons.title: Making a Budget
lessons.content: A budget is a plan for your money. It shows how much money you have and what you will spend it on. A good budget includes money for saving, spending, and sharing. Writing down what you spend helps you see where your money goes.

lessons.title: Smart Shopping
lessons.content: Smart shopping means comparing prices before buying. Look for sales, check different stores, and think about whether you really need something. Sometimes waiting a day before buying helps you decide if you really want it.

title: 6-8: Study Skills for Success
desc: Learn effective study strategies to improve your grades.

lessons.title: The Science of Learning
lessons.content: Your brain learns best when you study in short sessions, take breaks, and review material multiple times over several days. This is called spaced repetition. Cramming the night before a test does not work as well as studying a little bit each day.

lessons.title: Note-Taking Strategies
lessons.content: Good notes help you remember what you learned. Use the Cornell method: divide your page into a main section for notes, a smaller section for key words, and a summary at the bottom. Write notes in your own words, not just copying the textbook.

lessons.title: Time Management
lessons.content: Managing your time means planning when to study, do homework, and relax. Use a planner or calendar. Break big projects into smaller tasks. Set specific times for homework and stick to them. Avoid multitasking - focus on one thing at a time.

lessons.title: Test Preparation
lessons.content: Start studying for tests several days in advance. Review your notes, make flashcards, and practice with sample questions. Get a good night's sleep before the test. Eat a healthy breakfast. Being prepared reduces test anxiety.

lessons.title: Overcoming Procrastination
lessons.content: Procrastination is putting things off. To beat it: set small goals, use a timer for 25-minute study sessions (Pomodoro technique), remove distractions like your phone, and reward yourself when you finish tasks. Starting is the hardest part - just begin!

title: 6-8: Growth Mindset
desc: Learn how a growth mindset can help you succeed in school and life.

lessons.title: Fixed vs Growth Mindset
lessons.content: A fixed mindset means believing your abilities cannot change. A growth mindset means believing you can improve through effort and practice. People with a growth mindset embrace challenges, learn from mistakes, and persist when things get difficult.

lessons.title: The Power of 'Yet'
lessons.content: When you can't do something, add the word 'yet.' 'I can't do this... yet.' This simple word changes your mindset from 'I can't' to 'I can learn.' Your brain grows stronger every time you learn something new, just like a muscle.

lessons.title: Learning from Mistakes
lessons.content: Mistakes are not failures - they are opportunities to learn. Your brain actually grows more when you make a mistake and then figure out why. Don't be afraid to try hard things. Easy tasks don't help your brain grow.

lessons.title: Effort Over Talent
lessons.content: Natural talent exists, but effort matters more. People who work hard and practice consistently often outperform those who are naturally talented but don't try. Effort and practice build skills that talent alone cannot.

lessons.title: Setting Goals
lessons.content: Set specific, achievable goals. Instead of 'get better at math,' set 'improve my math grade by one letter this semester.' Break big goals into smaller steps. Celebrate progress along the way. Remember that improvement takes time and persistence.

title: 9-12: Career Exploration
desc: Explore career paths and learn how to prepare for your future.

lessons.title: Finding Your Path
lessons.content: Career exploration is about discovering what you enjoy and what you're good at. Your career path doesn't have to be decided right now, but exploring options early gives you time to prepare. Consider your interests, skills, values, and the lifestyle you want.

lessons.title: Education and Training
lessons.content: Different careers require different education. Some need a 4-year college degree, others need a 2-year associate degree, trade school, or certifications. Research what your interested careers require. Many high-paying careers don't require a 4-year degree.

lessons.title: Building Skills
lessons.content: Employers value soft skills like communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and adaptability. Build these through extracurricular activities, volunteering, part-time jobs, and group projects. Technical skills can be learned, but soft skills make you stand out.

lessons.title: Financial Literacy Basics
lessons.content: Understanding money is essential for any career. Learn about income, taxes, budgeting, saving, and investing. A good salary doesn't guarantee financial success if you don't manage your money wisely. Start building good financial habits now.

lessons.title: Creating a Resume
lessons.content: A resume is a summary of your skills, education, and experience. Start building yours early. Include part-time jobs, volunteer work, extracurricular activities, and relevant coursework. Tailor your resume to each job. Proofread carefully - errors make a bad impression.

title: 9-12: Mental Health and Wellness
desc: Learn about mental health, stress management, and self-care.

lessons.title: Understanding Mental Health
lessons.content: Mental health is just as important as physical health. It affects how we think, feel, and act. Mental health includes emotional, psychological, and social well-being. Everyone has mental health, and it's okay to need help. Mental health conditions are common and treatable.

lessons.title: Stress Management
lessons.content: Stress is a normal part of life, but too much stress can harm you. Healthy ways to manage stress include exercise, deep breathing, meditation, talking to friends, journaling, and getting enough sleep. Avoid unhealthy coping like substance use, which makes things worse long-term.

lessons.title: Recognizing Warning Signs
lessons.content: Warning signs of mental health struggles include persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, changes in sleep or appetite, difficulty concentrating, withdrawal from friends, and thoughts of self-harm. If you notice these signs in yourself or others, seek help from a counselor, teacher, or mental health professional.

lessons.title: Self-Care Strategies
lessons.content: Self-care means taking care of your physical and mental health. This includes getting 8-10 hours of sleep, eating nutritious food, exercising regularly, drinking water, spending time outdoors, maintaining friendships, and setting boundaries. Self-care is not selfish - it's necessary.

lessons.title: Seeking Help
lessons.content: Asking for help is a sign of strength, not weakness. Talk to a trusted adult, school counselor, or mental health professional. Resources include the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline (988) and Crisis Text Line (text HOME to 741741). You are never alone, and things can get better with support.
